results.bound: O(p) passes, expected space \widetilde{O}\left(\delta^{-1}\varepsilon^{-3.5}\left(\frac{m+T}{\sqrt{T}}\right)\right), mixed approximation (1+\varepsilon, \widetilde{O}(n^{1/2^p}))
results.quote: Let S be a stream of edges representing a simple graph G with n vertices, m edges and T triangles. Then there exists an O(p) pass algorithm that uses expected \widetilde{O}\left(\delta^{-1}\varepsilon^{-3.5}\left(\frac{m+T}{\sqrt{T}}\right)\right) space, and with probability 1-\delta-1/poly(n) outputs a mixed (1+\varepsilon,\widetilde{O}(n^{1/2^p})) approximation of T. The algorithm does not require any prior knowledge of T.

results.bound: O(log log n) passes, (1+\varepsilon, 0) mixed approximation, expected space \widetilde{O}(\delta^{-1}\varepsilon^{-3.5}(m+T)/\sqrt{T})
results.quote: LOGLOGPASS returns a \((1+\varepsilon,0)\) mixed approximation of T with probability at least \(1-\delta-1/poly(n)\), using \(\widetilde{O}(\delta^{-1}\varepsilon^{-3.5}(m+T)/\sqrt{T})\) expected space.

results.bound: \Omega(m/\sqrt{\beta}) space for (\alpha,\beta)-approximation; \Theta(m) space for multiplicative approximation for all T
results.quote: Let \alpha>1 and \beta>0 satisfy \beta<\sqrt{m/2} and 2(\alpha+1)\beta<m/4. Let A be a one-pass, parameter-free algorithm that returns an (\alpha,\beta)-approximation of T with failure probability 1/m^4 when the stream is in random order. Then A may require \Omega(m/\sqrt{\beta}) space even when run on an input for any T<m/4.
